summary: The English is sound in 5:15-5:18. Two renderings go against the normative commentators. In 5:13 the third and fourth types were made indicative ('one who gives, and others give too'), against Rambam's 'wants others to give'. In 5:14 'among those who go' goes against Bartenura and Rambam, who both read 'in the going to the house of study'. The senses were filled mechanically with '1': verbs got the root heading rather than the stem sense, names got the etymology header, and many tokens are linked to wrong homographs (Arba, Ain, Shem, Sacar, 'lamb' for זֶה, 'where?' for אֵין, 'ploughshare' for אֵת). These are repointed to the Jastrow entries the pack lists, or the sense is removed with a note. The model morphology is largely right. The patches fix two construct states missed (מַחֲלֹקֶת in 5:17), חֵטְא הָרַבִּים, the participle בָּא after אֵין, and the root and lemma of לְהִתְקַיֵּם; the 5:16 grammar wrongly called בְּטֵלָה a perfect.

patches.value: There are four types in giving charity. One who wants to give but wants others not to give has an evil eye toward what belongs to others. One who wants others to give but himself not to give has an evil eye toward his own. One who wants to give and wants others to give is pious. One who wants neither himself nor others to give is wicked.
patches.reason: The third and fourth types have the same modal imperfects as the second (יִתֵּן וְיִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים; לֹא יִתֵּן וְלֹא יִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים) with הָרוֹצֶה understood. The English supplied 'wants' in the second type but turned the third and fourth into facts ('One who gives, and others give too'), as if piety were others happening to give. Rambam (normative) says the pious man is not content that he alone shows mercy but wants others to show mercy too. That is a wish, so 'wants' must carry through.

patches.value: The mishnah gives the first two types no label beyond 'evil eye'; the English keeps this. In the second, third and fourth types the Hebrew has bare imperfects, and הָרוֹצֶה is understood from the first clause. The English supplies 'wants' in all three, as Rambam reads the third (the pious man is not content that he alone shows mercy but wants others to show it too). The pack's BDB entries for אַרְבַּע (Arba, a name), מִדָּה (tribute), עַיִן (Ain, a place) and אַחַר (the adverb 'after') are the wrong words. The tokens are pointed to the Jastrow entries the pack lists, or carry no sense.
patches.reason: The old note defended the indicative 'one who gives, and others give too', which the review corrects.

patches.value: There are four types in going to the house of study. One who goes but does not do: the reward of going is in his hand. One who does but does not go: the reward of doing is in his hand. One who goes and does is pious. One who neither goes nor does is wicked.
patches.reason: Both normative commentators read בְּהוֹלְכֵי as 'in the going to', not 'among those who go'. Bartenura on 5:13 says so explicitly ('וְכֵן בְּסָמוּךְ בְּהוֹלְכֵי לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, הַיְנוּ בַּהֲלִיכַת בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ'), since one of the four never goes. Rambam on this mishnah says the same: 'רוצה בו ההליכה לבית המדרש יש בה ארבע מדות'. The translator applied this reading in 5:13 ('in giving charity') and cited it in the phrase literal, but the English did not follow it.

value: The first saying is a conditional without a particle: בָּטֵל דָּבָר, בְּטֵלָה אַהֲבָה, '(when) the thing ceases, the love ceases'. Each predicate stands before its subject.

בְּטֵלָה is the feminine singular of the stative participle (verbal adjective) בָּטֵל, 'ceasing, void', and agrees with אַהֲבָה. The feminine perfect would be בָּטְלָה. The masculine בָּטֵל agrees with דָּבָר; it can be read as the same participle or as the stative perfect 'has ceased'.
וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ is 'and that which is not' (ש + אֵין + 3rd fem. sing. suffix): the headless relative stands for 'a love which ...'.
Question and answer: אֵיזוֹ הִיא ... זוֹ ..., 'which is ...? This is ...'; אֵיזוֹ is the feminine of אֵיזֶה, 'which'.
אַהֲבַת is the construct of אַהֲבָה: 'love of'.
patches.reason: The notes called both forms perfects ('the perfect בָּטֵל, twice'). בְּטֵלָה cannot be a perfect: the feminine perfect is בָּטְלָה. It is the feminine participle/verbal adjective, as the morphology has it.

patches.value: דָּבָר is kept as 'a thing' because it is general: the commentators explain it as the cause or object on which the love depends (beauty in Amnon's case; a lasting purpose for David and Jonathan). The pack's BDB entry for זֶה ('lamb') is the wrong word, so the demonstratives point to Jastrow's זֶה, 'this'. For בָּטֵל, Jastrow's sense 2 ('to cease to exist') is the right one; Jastrow cites this mishnah there. The BDB entry for תָּמָר has David's daughter at sense 4.
patches.reason: The old note said תָּמָר's first sense is a place name. It is the name's meaning ('palm-tree'); the place is sense 7. The note also called the entries for זֶה and בָּטֵל 'the closest available', but the pack lists the right ones.

patches.value: Whoever makes the many meritorious, no sin comes through him. And whoever causes the many to sin, they do not give him the means to repent. Moses was meritorious and made the many meritorious; the merit of the many rests on him, as it is said, Deuteronomy 33: "He performed the righteousness of the LORD, and His judgments with Israel." Jeroboam sinned and caused the many to sin; the sin of the many rests on him, as it is said, 1 Kings 15: "For the sins of Jeroboam (son of Nebat), which he sinned and which he caused Israel to sin."
patches.reason: The mishnah puts בֶּן נְבָט in brackets (it is not in every text of the quotation). The English now keeps the brackets, so nothing appears unmarked.

patches.value: 'Merit' (זְכוּת) is kept as one English word through the mishnah for the pun on זָכָה / זִכָּה. תָּלוּי בּוֹ is rendered 'rests on him' to keep the sense 'depends on, is attributed to'; 'hangs' is given in the literal line. The impersonal 'they do not give him the means' is kept as an impersonal plural, as in the Hebrew. The pack lists no entry for the verb חָטָא or for the Hiphil of ספק, so those tokens carry no sense.
patches.reason: The old note cited misfit senses for שֵׁם and יָשַׁב, which do not occur in this mishnah.
